title: Doctrine, sources and drift
scope: The genesis documents the system was built from, their authority, and how to treat the gap between them and the system as built. The commander's rule governs the topic: the day-one sources are not canon that may never be drifted from, divergence between them and the system as built is not to be measured, and the question to ask of the canon instead is what has superseded what. Excludes the library that stores them (see the-library-and-records).

statements.statement: Below is a local source of guides and manuals for orchestration patterns
statements.context: The opening prompt of the first build run, introducing the eleven source pages.

statements.statement: I have in here library/source/orchestrator-pattern the source of this whole method. Endings guide is a very good wayfinder, also runlog, pointing us to the true foundations of the method.
statements.context: Redirecting a problem-hunting session to the source pages.

statements.statement: I discovered problems and divergence from the source documents, the original agent used as their source of truth (the source is not perfect and has a few contradictions, but the human knows which path to take
statements.context: Opening brief for the rebuild, on the standing of the source.

statements.statement: The orchestrator when building this, had no "flightcrew" system to use. so used his own "system". nearly everything slipped in due to "clean slate". no need to state it in every problem file.
statements.context: Explaining why the built system diverges from the method in so many places.

statements.statement: this is iterative improvement, "abandon failed runs", eventually it will outstrip the "source" as it is improved progressively.
statements.context: Asked what happens when the system and the source disagree.

statements.statement: The orchestration principles where derived from those sources with a bit of "fitment" they are very important documents that the original all in one builder tried to replicate the system from. Systems like flightcrew grow organicly but these types of genesis documents are important to update and maintain over time, especially for a pilot who needs to understand where things are at.
statements.context: Written advice on why the genesis documents are maintained rather than archived.

statements.statement: I mentioned the departure because I didn't want the original day 1 resources to be considered as cannon never to be drifted. So therefore I don't want divergence measured either. The commanders' advice is to understand that the system drifts slowly as it is used and improved in real time. And not to be reluctant to change your understanding as it shifts. also look for relevance in the cannon, has a claim superseded another.
statements.context: Written advice rejecting a record that measured how far the system had departed from its sources.

statements.statement: Doctrine discovery and integration should be an important part of the cockpit furnishing mission.
statements.context: Written advice, after the recon team under-read the doctrine.
